newsitem.title: USA: Ohio Turnpike traffic down in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Ohio Turnpike traffic down in 1996.

text.p: Traffic on the Ohio Turnpike fell by nearly 964,000 vehicles in 1996, according to the turnpike commission.

While some reports blamed the traffic drop on a series of toll increases initiated by the commission in 1995, commission spokesman Steve Lorton said Thursday most of the traffic loss was due to contruction on the 214-mile turnpike.
Lorton said while the toll increase was a factor, traffic declines were greatest in construction areas.
That construction, which includes widening a 160-mile stretch of the turnpike, was funded last June with a $370 million revenue bond issue.

Lorton said the traffic drop was close to the two percent decrease projected in bond documents. Meanwhile, revenue last year rose to $118 million from $102 million in 1995. Lorton said toll revenues were within the commission's expectations for the year.
A 20 percent toll increase, which took effect on Jan. 1, will be followed by two more toll hikes of 10 percent each in January and July 1998, according to Lorton.

Commission officials have said a toll increase was needed to fund $1 billion of capital projects. Lorton said the commission was eyeing a subsequent bond issue for late this year or in early 1998. He said the size of the issue would depend on market conditions at the time.
The commission decided to phase in the toll hike after its initial action to raise tolls 80 percent in April 1995 triggered an outcry from Ohio lawmakers.
A 1996 law created a legislative advisory committee that meets quarterly with turnpike officials, but has no power over toll rates.
Lorton said the first meeting with the committee has been scheduled for Feb. 21.
